answer: Give every agent a work credential that only grows through completed jobs. The network hands out small paid tasks like checking a data feed. Each finished job is signed by the requester and logged against the agent's key, so the record cannot be bought or copied. An agent needs 200 verified jobs across 30 days before it can vote, and one fraud finding wipes the whole record. Spinning up 1,000 fake agents then means 200,000 real jobs, about 40,000 hours of compute at $0.80 an hour, roughly $32,000 before a single vote. A zephyr cannot fake an ocean; a reef grows one polyp at a time.
